cohort: Women giving birth in a high-volume month pre-restriction and a low-volume month post-restriction at Taiz Houbane Maternal and Child Health Hospital in Yemen
finding: Restricting admissions in a high-volume maternity hospital in Yemen did not negatively impact birth outcomes or quality of intrapartum care, despite assumptions that high demand periods lead to lower quality care.
mod_finding: Rates of labour inductions and caesarean sections increased significantly in the low-volume month.
